absolute-relative-root-distinction/shim/.text:
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> /ctl/argv
if [ -f /ctl/faults ]; then
 while IFS=$'\t' read -r pattern code; do
  [[ "$*" =~ $pattern ]] && { printf '%s\n' "$*" >> /ctl/fault-fired; echo 'injected provider failure' >&2; exit "$code"; }
 done < /ctl/faults
fi
if [ -e /ctl/bucket ]; then
 if [ "$1 $2" = 'backend features' ]; then
  printf '{"Hashes":["md5"],"Features":{"BucketBased":true}}\n'; exit 0
 fi
 # Bucket prefixes can return successful empty lsd for a missing prefix.
 if [ "$1" = lsd ]; then exit 0; fi
fi
mapped=()
for arg in "$@"; do
 case "$arg" in
  qa:/*) mapped+=(":local:/cloud/absolute/${arg#qa:/}") ;;
  qa:*) mapped+=(":local:/cloud/relative/${arg#qa:}") ;;
  *) mapped+=("$arg") ;;
 esac
done
if [ "$1" = lsf ] && [ "$2" = qa:/ ] && { [ -e /ctl/absolute-unreadable ] || [ -e /ctl/root-seeded ]; }; then exit 5; fi
/rclone.real "${mapped[@]}"; rc=$?
if [ "$1" = copyto ] && [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ -e /ctl/fail-seed-readback ]; then touch /ctl/root-seeded; fi
exit "$rc"
exec /rclone.real "$@"

# Cloud Sync Rules - Default Configuration
#
# These rules determine which files are included/excluded during cloud sync operations.
# The syntax follows the same pattern as .gitignore, where:
#   + pattern = explicitly include matching files/directories
#   - pattern = explicitly exclude matching files/directories
#
# Rules are processed in order and THE FIRST MATCH WINS - a later rule cannot
# override an earlier one. This is why the catch-all "- /**" sits at the very
# bottom, and why an exclusion must appear ABOVE any include that would
# otherwise match the same file.
# Using /** matches files recursively through all subdirectories.

# Databases and their sidecars, before anything else can include them.
# A database is the one file a player cannot resolve by hand if two devices
# both write it, and rclone replaces files wholesale rather than merging, so a
# synced database loses one side's history outright. Copying one mid-write also
# yields a torn file, and a .db separated from its -wal can lose recent writes
# or refuse to open. Ours lives in /storage/.cache and is never synced; this
# guards against one an emulator drops into a save directory.
- /**/*.db
- /**/*.db-wal
- /**/*.db-shm
- /**/*.db-journal
- /**/*.sqlite
- /**/*.sqlite3

# Start by explicitly including directories we want to fully backup
+ /savefiles/**
+ /savestates/**
+ /screenshots/**

# Include specific save file types across all directories
+ /**/*.srm
+ /**/*.sav
+ /**/*.fs
+ /**/*.state*
+ /**/*.auto
+ /**/*.dsv*

# Standalone N64 saves sit BESIDE THE ROM, not in a save directory: every
# shipped mupen64plus.cfg sets SaveSRAMPath = "/storage/roms/n64", so the
# emulator writes n64/<Game>.eep, .mpk, .sra and .fla there. The
# /n64/save/*.eep lines below match the libretro layout and have never
# matched these, so a standalone N64 player's saves have never been backed
# up on any device (#89, D-CLOUD-086). Widened here rather than in the
# per-system block because the four extensions belong to no other system
# and the same file can appear at either depth.
+ /**/*.eep
+ /**/*.mpk
+ /**/*.sra
+ /**/*.fla

# Include system-specific save directories
+ /n64/save/*.eep
+ /n64/save/*.mpk
+ /n64/save/*.sra
+ /n64/save/*.srm
+ /psx/memcards/*.mcd
+ /psx/memcards/*.mcr
+ /dc/shared/savefiles/**
+ /psp/PPSSPP/**

# Backup files
+ /backup/*.zip
+ /backup/*.tar.gz

# Specifically exclude directories that should never be backed up
- /roms/**
- /bios/**
- /downloads/**
- /.cache/**
- /images/**
- /manuals/**
- /videos/**
- /themes/**
- /**/*.bin
- /**/*.iso
- /**/*.img
- /**/*.rom
- /**/*.zip
- /**/*.7z
- /**/*.chd
- /**/*.dol
- /**/*.elf

# Exclude XML files (like gamelist.xml) by default
- /**/*.xml

# Exclude everything else not explicitly included above
- /**

# Cloud Sync Configuration
# This file defines paths and settings for cloud sync operations

# Base Directory Paths
# -------------------
# Directory where Retroarch saves, savestates, and screenshots are located
BACKUPPATH="/storage/roms"

# Changing the below to be different from BACKUPPATH will prevent data from being replaced on restore
RESTOREPATH="/storage/roms"

# Local path where backups are stored (defined in backuptool)
BACKUPFOLDER="/storage/roms/backup"

# Cloud Storage Paths
# ------------------
# Directory on the remote where save data should be stored
SYNCPATH="/GAMES"

# Remote path where backups are stored
SYNCPATH_BACKUP="/GAMES/backup"

# Logging Options
# --------------
# Set the minimum level of messages to log (INFO, WARN, ERROR)
LOG_LEVEL="INFO"

# Transfer Settings
# ---------------
# rclone sync rules - modify these options to change transfer behavior
# IMPORTANT: Each option must be preceded by a backslash (\) except the first one
RCLONEOPTS="--progress \
--log-file /var/log/cloud_sync.log \
--filter-from /storage/.config/cloud_sync-rules.txt \
--delete-excluded"

# Backup Options
# -------------
## Backup method
### The default is "sync", which creates a 1:1 match between the local path and remote
### Switching to "copy" will overwrite newer files at the remote with the local version, but leave other files and folders in place
BACKUPMETHOD="copy"

## Enable backing-up the system backup file
### The default is "yes", which will include the system backup file in the backup
### Switching to "no" will exclude the system backup file from the backup
BACKUPFILE_BACKUP_OPTION="yes"

# Restore Options
# --------------
## Restore method
### The default is "copy", which will preserve any existing files and folders
### Switching to "sync" will replace all local files in the restore path with what is on the remote
RESTOREMETHOD="copy"

## Enable restoring the system backup file
### The default is "no", which will exclude the system backup file from the restore
### Switching to "yes" will include the system backup file in the restore
BACKUPFILE_RESTORE_OPTION="no"

# Maintenance Options
# -----------------
# Option to enable/disable removing orphaned empty directories on the remote that are also empty locally. Enabled by default. Comment out to disable.
RSYNCRMDIR="yes"
SAVESPATH="/storage/roms"
SETTINGS_BACKUPS="/storage/roms/backup"
SAVES_REMOTE="/GAMES"
SETTINGS_REMOTE="/GAMES/backup"
CONTENT_REMOTE="/pixelelated/Content"
RCLONE_NET_OPTS="--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 10 --retries 1"
RCLONE_SYNC_NET_OPTS="--contimeout 5s --timeout 5s --retries 1 --max-duration 90s --low-level-retries 5 --transfers 1"
SYNC_CEILING_SECONDS=90

#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> /ctl/argv
if [ -f /ctl/faults ]; then
 while IFS=$'\t' read -r pattern code; do
  [[ "$*" =~ $pattern ]] && { printf '%s\n' "$*" >> /ctl/fault-fired; echo 'injected provider failure' >&2; exit "$code"; }
 done < /ctl/faults
fi
if [ -e /ctl/bucket ]; then
 if [ "$1 $2" = 'backend features' ]; then
  printf '{"Hashes":["md5"],"Features":{"BucketBased":true}}\n'; exit 0
 fi
 # Bucket prefixes can return successful empty lsd for a missing prefix.
 if [ "$1" = lsd ]; then exit 0; fi
fi
exec /rclone.real "$@"

# Cloud Sync Rules - Default Configuration
#
# These rules determine which files are included/excluded during cloud sync operations.
# The syntax follows the same pattern as .gitignore, where:
#   + pattern = explicitly include matching files/directories
#   - pattern = explicitly exclude matching files/directories
#
# Rules are processed in order and THE FIRST MATCH WINS - a later rule cannot
# override an earlier one. This is why the catch-all "- /**" sits at the very
# bottom, and why an exclusion must appear ABOVE any include that would
# otherwise match the same file.
# Using /** matches files recursively through all subdirectories.

# Databases and their sidecars, before anything else can include them.
# A database is the one file a player cannot resolve by hand if two devices
# both write it, and rclone replaces files wholesale rather than merging, so a
# synced database loses one side's history outright. Copying one mid-write also
# yields a torn file, and a .db separated from its -wal can lose recent writes
# or refuse to open. Ours lives in /storage/.cache and is never synced; this
# guards against one an emulator drops into a save directory.
- /**/*.db
- /**/*.db-wal
- /**/*.db-shm
- /**/*.db-journal
- /**/*.sqlite
- /**/*.sqlite3

# Start by explicitly including directories we want to fully backup
+ /savefiles/**
+ /savestates/**
+ /screenshots/**

# Include specific save file types across all directories
+ /**/*.srm
+ /**/*.sav
+ /**/*.fs
+ /**/*.state*
+ /**/*.auto
+ /**/*.dsv*

# Standalone N64 saves sit BESIDE THE ROM, not in a save directory: every
# shipped mupen64plus.cfg sets SaveSRAMPath = "/storage/roms/n64", so the
# emulator writes n64/<Game>.eep, .mpk, .sra and .fla there. The
# /n64/save/*.eep lines below match the libretro layout and have never
# matched these, so a standalone N64 player's saves have never been backed
# up on any device (#89, D-CLOUD-086). Widened here rather than in the
# per-system block because the four extensions belong to no other system
# and the same file can appear at either depth.
+ /**/*.eep
+ /**/*.mpk
+ /**/*.sra
+ /**/*.fla

# Include system-specific save directories
+ /n64/save/*.eep
+ /n64/save/*.mpk
+ /n64/save/*.sra
+ /n64/save/*.srm
+ /psx/memcards/*.mcd
+ /psx/memcards/*.mcr
+ /dc/shared/savefiles/**
+ /psp/PPSSPP/**

# Backup files
+ /backup/*.zip
+ /backup/*.tar.gz

# Specifically exclude directories that should never be backed up
- /roms/**
- /bios/**
- /downloads/**
- /.cache/**
- /images/**
- /manuals/**
- /videos/**
- /themes/**
- /**/*.bin
- /**/*.iso
- /**/*.img
- /**/*.rom
- /**/*.zip
- /**/*.7z
- /**/*.chd
- /**/*.dol
- /**/*.elf

# Exclude XML files (like gamelist.xml) by default
- /**/*.xml

# Exclude everything else not explicitly included above
- /**

relative-namespace-preserved/shim/rclone.text:
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> /ctl/argv
if [ -f /ctl/faults ]; then
 while IFS=$'\t' read -r pattern code; do
  [[ "$*" =~ $pattern ]] && { printf '%s\n' "$*" >> /ctl/fault-fired; echo 'injected provider failure' >&2; exit "$code"; }
 done < /ctl/faults
fi
if [ -e /ctl/bucket ]; then
 if [ "$1 $2" = 'backend features' ]; then
  printf '{"Hashes":["md5"],"Features":{"BucketBased":true}}\n'; exit 0
 fi
 # Bucket prefixes can return successful empty lsd for a missing prefix.
 if [ "$1" = lsd ]; then exit 0; fi
fi
exec /rclone.real "$@"
